# clavis trust add

<p class="cli-lead">Check a server&#39;s certificate and trust it</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis trust add [SERVER] [flags]
```

</div>

Connect to the server, show its certificate (subject, expiry, SHA-256
fingerprint) and ask whether to trust it. Without an argument it uses
the server from `--server` or `.clavis.yaml`.

With `--fingerprint`, nothing is asked: the certificate is trusted if it
matches, and refused otherwise. Both the certificate fingerprint and the
public key fingerprint are accepted, with or without colons.

If the certificate is already trusted (by the system or by an earlier
pin), `trust add` says so and changes nothing.

## Examples

```sh
clavis trust add https://192.168.1.20
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Non-interactive</p>

```sh
clavis trust add clavis.lan --fingerprint 9e1c…f9
```

## Flags

<dl class="cli-flags">
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-fingerprint"><dt><code>--fingerprint string</code></dt><dd>expected SHA-256 of the certificate or its public key; trusts without asking</dd></div>
</dl>

## Details

In a script without a terminal, `trust add` without `--fingerprint` fails and prints the fingerprint to check, instead of trusting blindly.
